cards.advises: Uzbekistan should invite its mining, textile and telecom companies to co-finance rural clinics and family doctors, so essential care reaches every family. With super intelligence, a family doctor in a mahalla clinic can follow each patient’s blood pressure and sugar at home.

cards.title: Solar and Clean Stoves for Vanuatu
cards.challenge: In Vanuatu, 65.5% of people have electricity and only 20% cook with clean fuels and technology.
cards.advises: Vanuatu should invite private investors to finance solar lights and clean cookstoves sold through island shops and cooperatives, with the cost recovered from the kerosene and wood families no longer buy, so every home has power and cooks without smoke. With super intelligence, each island’s demand can be planned, so equipment arrives before it is needed.

cards.title: Care Across the Islands of Vanuatu
cards.challenge: Vanuatu scores 52 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
cards.advises: Vanuatu should finance provincial hospitals, health centres and aid posts with the Asian Development Bank and the World Bank, so essential care reaches every island. With super intelligence, an aid post worker can consult a doctor in Port Vila by satellite.

cards.title: Kava, Cocoa and Coconuts
cards.challenge: 36.9% of people in Vanuatu live on less than US$4.20 a day.
cards.advises: Vanuatu should invite its tourism and food companies to buy kava, cocoa, coconut and beef from local farmers under fair contracts, so families climb above the poverty line. With super intelligence, every farmer can see the prices buyers offer before the harvest.

cards.title: Work for Every Venezuelan Family
cards.challenge: 33.1% of people in Venezuela live below the national poverty line.
cards.advises: Venezuela should invite its oil, food and telecom companies into training and hiring partnerships, with credit for small suppliers, so every family earns above the poverty line. With super intelligence, each Venezuelan returning home can find work that uses the skills learned abroad.

cards.title: Hospitals Restocked for Venezuela
cards.challenge: Venezuela scores 75 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
cards.advises: Venezuela should finance medicines, equipment and the repair of hospitals with CAF, so essential care reaches every family. With super intelligence, every hospital can forecast the medicines it will need, so shelves are restocked before they empty.

cards.title: The Venezuelan Diaspora Schools Fund
cards.challenge: Only 83.2% of young people in Venezuela complete lower secondary school.
cards.advises: Venezuela should invite its diaspora and impact investors into a fund for teachers, school meals and second-chance classes, so every young person completes lower secondary school. With super intelligence, teachers abroad can teach students at home on screen.

cards.title: Safe Water from the Red River to the Delta
cards.challenge: Only 58.6% of people in Vietnam use safely managed drinking water.
cards.advises: Vietnam should finance new treatment plants and piped village water for the Mekong Delta and the northern mountains with the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, so every family drinks safe water. With super intelligence, salt water entering the delta can be forecast, so every plant keeps drawing fresh water.

cards.title: Clinics for Every Commune
cards.challenge: Vietnam scores 71 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
cards.advises: Vietnam should invite private investors to finance commune health stations and district hospitals in partnership with the national health insurance, so essential care reaches every family. With super intelligence, a commune health station can share tests with a provincial hospital at once.

cards.title: Factories for the Uplands
cards.challenge: 21.5% of people in Vietnam live on less than US$8.30 a day.
cards.advises: Vietnam should invite its electronics, textile and food companies to open training and supplier partnerships in the upland provinces, so every family earns above the poverty line. With super intelligence, each young worker in the uplands can learn a skilled trade online before the factory opens.

cards.title: Solar Power for Yemen
cards.challenge: People in Yemen use about 129 kWh of electricity a year, against the Living Line of 1,000 kWh, and 47% cook with clean fuels.
cards.advises: Yemen should finance solar power for homes, hospitals and water pumps with the Islamic Development Bank and the World Bank, so every family has power. With super intelligence, solar power can be sent first to water pumps and clinics, so they keep working through every outage.

cards.title: Bread and Harvests for Yemen
cards.challenge: 73% of people in Yemen are moderately or severely food insecure.
cards.advises: Yemen should invite its food importers, millers and traders to co-finance local harvests, storage and wheat reserves, so every household eats well. With super intelligence, food prices and stocks can be watched in every market, so shortages are met before they become hunger.

cards.title: Clinics That Stay Open
cards.challenge: Yemen scores 43 of 100 on the WHO index of essential health service coverage.
cards.advises: Yemen should invite its diaspora and impact investors into a fund that keeps clinics staffed, powered and stocked with medicines, so essential care reaches every family. With super intelligence, each clinic can forecast what it will need, so it never closes for want of supplies.

cards.title: Copper for Clean Kitchens
cards.challenge: Only 10% of people in Zambia cook with clean fuels and technology.
cards.advises: Zambia should invite its copper companies to finance gas, electric and efficient stoves for the homes that cook with charcoal, so every family cooks without smoke and the forests are spared. With super intelligence, charcoal sales and stove use can be tracked town by town, so the switch to clean cooking is measured as it happens.

cards.title: Enterprise Along the Copperbelt
cards.challenge: 81.4% of people in Zambia live on less than US$4.20 a day.
cards.advises: Zambia should invite private investors and its pension funds into a fund for small businesses that supply the mines and farms, with credit guarantees, so families climb above the poverty line. With super intelligence, each small supplier on the Copperbelt can see the tenders the mines will issue next.

cards.title: Irrigation for Zambian Harvests
cards.challenge: 45.8% of people in Zambia are moderately or severely food insecure.
cards.advises: Zambia should finance irrigation, storage and crop insurance for small farms with the African Development Bank and the World Bank, so every household eats well even in a drought. With super intelligence, each farm’s irrigation can be scheduled to the hour, so scarce water reaches every crop.

cards.title: Safe Water for Harare and Every Town
cards.challenge: Only 25.5% of people in Zimbabwe use safely managed drinking water.
cards.advises: Zimbabwe should finance water treatment and network repairs for Harare and its towns with the African Development Bank and the World Bank, so every family drinks safe water. With super intelligence, every network can be tested for contamination, so outbreaks are stopped before they start.

cards.title: Irrigation for the Communal Lands
cards.challenge: 70.1% of people in Zimbabwe are moderately or severely food insecure.
cards.advises: Zimbabwe should invite private investors into a fund for irrigation, seeds and storage on the communal lands, so every household eats well even in a dry year. With super intelligence, each field can be advised when to plant and how much to water.

cards.title: Minerals for Enterprise
cards.challenge: 64.6% of people in Zimbabwe live on less than US$4.20 a day.
cards.advises: Zimbabwe should invite its lithium, platinum and gold companies to buy goods and services from local firms, with training and credit, so families climb above the poverty line. With super intelligence, each local firm can be matched to the supplies the mines need.
